reason: Both pinpoint the identical root cause: sanitize_label's None-guard uses a bare `return` (returning None) instead of `return \"\"`, violating the declared `-> str` contract. Both also identify the same downstream consequence category — callers that treat the result as a string (ground truth: html.escape() in export.py's community-legend rendering; reviewer: .encode()/len()/concatenation generally) crash with an AttributeError/TypeError because they receive None instead of \"\". The reviewer's description is a broader generalization of the failure scenario rather than a different bug, but the mechanism (bare return → None leak) and the failure mode (string-op crash on None) match the ground truth.
